answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-bonded identity: before an agent may transact, it locks a refundable deposit in shared escrow, like a single opal set in resin rather than cheap pigment spread thin across paper. Spinning up ten thousand sock-puppets then costs ten thousand bonds, while an honest agent stakes once. Misbehavior triggers slashing, so the whisper of free fake identities dies out - every identity carries real, seizable cost.
